registers.name: CONTROL
registers.description: Enable/arm control plus write-one-pulse fault clear and mode bits. Writing bit0=1 enables the controller, bit1=1 arms request issuance, and bit2=1 clears latched faults. Bits [7:4] hold the operating mode. Unused bits read as 0.

fields.name: arm
fields.description: Arms the controller to issue requests when enabled and no request is pending.

fields.name: fault_clear
fields.description: Write 1 to clear latched fault state and fault summary bits.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: Operating mode bits copied into outbound request metadata.

registers.name: TIMEOUT
registers.description: Watchdog timeout threshold in cycles. The implementation uses the low 16 bits as the active threshold; a value of 0 is treated as the minimum legal timeout per RTL policy.

fields.name: timeout_cycles
fields.description: Maximum cycles to wait for a matching completed response before timeout fault is latched.

fields.name: min_cmd
fields.description: Lower bound applied to validated actuator command proposals.

fields.name: max_cmd
fields.description: Upper bound applied to validated actuator command proposals.

registers.name: STATUS
registers.description: Live status bits and fault visibility. This register is synchronously updated and reflects the current controller state and latched faults.

fields.name: armed
fields.description: Indicates the controller is both enabled and armed.

fields.name: pending_request
fields.description: Indicates a request has been issued and is awaiting a valid response.

fields.name: response_valid_seen
fields.description: Indicates at least one response-valid event has been observed for the current transaction window.

fields.name: fault_latched
fields.description: Indicates one or more fault bits are latched.

fields.name: stale_reject
fields.description: Set when a response is rejected as stale or sequence-mismatched.

fields.name: timeout_fault
fields.description: Set when the watchdog expires before a valid completed response is accepted.

fields.name: malformed_response
fields.description: Set when the inbound response fails format or completion validation.

fields.name: clamp_saturation
fields.description: Set when the accepted command required clamping to min or max limits.

fields.name: sequence_error
fields.description: Set when a response sequence number does not match the outstanding request.

fields.name: configuration_error
fields.description: Set when CSR configuration is inconsistent, such as min_cmd greater than max_cmd.

sources.name: FAULT_LATCHED
sources.description: Optional software-visible fault indication derived from STATUS.fault_latched and FAULTS.fault_flags.

init_sequence.action: Write CLAMP_MIN and CLAMP_MAX with a valid range, then write TIMEOUT with a nonzero threshold and configure any desired mode bits in CONTROL.
Write sequence seed and operating metadata through the reachable CSR map defined by DIGITAL_SPEC_JSON; then write CONTROL with enable=1 and arm=1.
Poll STATUS until armed=1 and pending_request transitions as requests are issued.

polling_sequence.action: Poll STATUS for pending_request, fault_latched, and individual fault bits.
Read FAULTS at 0x24 for the latched 8-bit fault summary when fault_latched is set.
Read MMIO-visible configuration registers to confirm programmed timeout and clamp settings if needed.

irq_sequence.action: If fault indication is wired to software interrupt handling, service the fault by reading STATUS and FAULTS.
Write CONTROL.fault_clear=1 to clear latched faults after the condition has been acknowledged and corrected.
Re-arm with CONTROL.enable=1 and CONTROL.arm=1 only after configuration is valid.

consistency_notes: The register map is compatible with DIGITAL_SPEC_JSON and uses the documented 32-bit synchronous CSR/MMIO interface.
All registers listed in DIGITAL_SPEC_JSON are reachable through RTL decode; no inaccessible software-visible registers are declared.
The outbound request and inbound response streams remain separate from the CSR/MMIO control-plane interface.
This JSON intentionally reflects the no-command-fallback contract by omitting any fallback command register or fallback output semantics.
The fault summary register FAULTS at offset 0x24 is included because it is explicitly declared in DIGITAL_SPEC_JSON and reachable through RTL decode.
